chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
"If the witnesses testify against the adulterer that he had sat with her in the manner of a man with his wife, the hadd is carried out upon them both."
He said: "And ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say: O Allah, if You give me power over al-Mughīrah, I will surely stone him with stones."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These reports that we mentioned last, which include mention of making the hadd obligatory upon two persons sleeping in one garment, do not contradict what we presented earlier from the reports concerning the obligation of taʿzīr, because the mention of hadd in them is to be understood as the hadd of taʿzīr, since that may be called hadd by way of figurative usage. There is no mention in any of them of the quantity of the hadd, and when they can bear that meaning, the contradiction falls away. As for the differing amounts of taʿzīr, that is according to what the Imam sees fit, from thirty lashes up to ninety-nine lashes, according to what he considers more proper and more deterrent; thus he does it and carries it out accordingly, and the matter in that is entrusted to him.

key_terms.التَّعْزِيرِ: a discretionary disciplinary punishment determined by authority
key_terms.الزَّانِي: the adulterer or fornicator accused of zina
key_terms.الشُّهُودُ: the witnesses whose testimony establishes the case
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the authority entrusted with determining the suitable level of taʿzīr
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the prescribed legal punishment mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْمُغِيرَةِ: al-Mughīrah, the individual named in the statement of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.سَوْطاً: lashes as the unit of corporal punishment

ai.seo_question: How do Shia hadith reconcile reports about hadd and taʿzīr in zina-related cases?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the legal establishment of the hadd for zina upon sufficient witness testimony and also transmits a statement from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding al-Mughīrah. The compiler then explains that reports mentioning hadd in related cases may be interpreted as referring to taʿzīr, with its amount left to the Imam’s judgment according to what is most suitable and deterrent.
